narrative:
The model determined that you have a 63% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is well above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and the presence of a guarantor. 

Your requested duration of 48 months was more than twice as long as the average of approved applicants (19 months). Longer loan terms strongly increase the assessed risk, pushing the prediction toward denial. Your checking account, which is currently in negative balance, is also relatively uncommon among approved applicants and added further weight toward viewing you as higher risk. These two elements were the most influential reasons for the rejection.

The fact that you have a guarantor worked in your favor and pulled the prediction somewhat toward approval. However, this positive effect was not large enough to overcome the impact of the longer duration and negative account status.

To improve your chances on a future application, consider applying for a shorter loan term, wait until your checking account balance is positive, or explore options that do not require such a large amount. These changes would directly address the main reasons the model saw you as higher risk. (218 words)
